title: Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2025 Measures No. 1) Bill 2025
short_title: Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2025 Measures No. 1) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would confirm the lawfulness of past and future government actions concerning offshore processing and certain visa refusals.
It would amend the Migration Act 1958 to remove the requirement for procedural fairness when the government makes deals with foreign countries on third country reception arrangements.
It would also validate visa decisions that were overturned by a court because the minister relied on a now-overruled High Court ruling about indefinite detention.
changes: The bill would make the rules of natural justice inapplicable to entering or preparing third country reception arrangements with foreign countries.
It would validate any past actions taken in relation to those arrangements that were invalid only because natural justice was not observed.
It would validate certain protection visa refusal decisions that were set aside by the Full Federal Court in the AJN23 case.
summary.affected: non-citizens subject to removal pathway arrangements, and protection visa applicants whose decisions were influenced by the now-overruled Al-Kateb ruling

divisions.question: The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-09-01.108.3): > *That the Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2025 Measures No. 1) Bill 2025 be referred to the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights for consideration and an advisory report.*
Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2025 Measures No. 1) Bill 2025 - First Reading - Put the question

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2025-09-03.239.1) *"that the bill may proceed without formalities.*" ### What does this motion need? According to the [parliamentary procedure handbook](https://www.aph.gov.au/About_Parliament/Senate/Practice_and_Procedure/aso/so113), the motion "*that the bill may proceed with formalities*": > *shall have the effect of suspending any requirements for stages of the passage of the bill or bills to take place on different days, for notice of motions for such stages, and for the printing and certification of the bill or bills during passage*
